subject: Pilot priority band request — Acme Robotics dedicated pool
messages:
From: Jeffrey Turner <jeffrey.turner@acme.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tony Liu <tony.liu@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request — short priority band for Q2 pilot

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to move to a week-long pilot. One ask that came up in our internal planning: for the pilot workload we need a guaranteed priority band (a slice of dedicated GPU pool capacity) to avoid noisy neighbors during the 4-hour daily inference window.

Rough details: 2x A40-equivalent slots (or equivalent throughput) reserved between 14:00-18:00 PST for 7 business days starting 2027-04-05. We understand this is an exception to the usual autoscale policy — willing to sign a short SOW and cover incremental charges.

Can you confirm feasibility and next steps (paperwork, provisioning lead time)? I attached a short pilot objectives doc (pilot-sla-proposal.pdf).

Appreciate it —
Jeffrey

--
Jeffrey Turner
Head of Product, Acme Robotics
jo: +1-415-555-0182
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jeffrey Turner <jeffrey.turner@acme.ai>, Tony Liu <tony.liu@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — short priority band for Q2 pilot

Jeffrey — thanks. Looping in capacity and ops so we can give a technical + timeline answer.

Quick notes:
- We can support short-duration reserved capacity for pilots but need to validate pool topology and any SLA deviations.
- Two parts to resolve: (1) allocation + autoscale exception for the 2x slots during the window, and (2) commercial terms for a short commitment.

Marissa/Marcus/Hannah — can you review the ask and confirm what footprint we can promise, any gating constraints (other reserved pools, planned maintenance windows), and the minimal lead time? If there are security or tenancy concerns (private routing or VPC peering) please flag.

Jeffrey — forwarding the pilot-sla-proposal.pdf to the team.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jeffrey Turner <jeffrey.turner@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — Pilot priority band sizing and carveout proposal

Neha —

Thanks for the loop. Read the pilot brief. Proposal from Product/Revenue side:
- Offer a temporary "priority band" carved out of the east-us dedicated pool: 2 GPU-equivalent slots for 7 business days, daily 14:00-18:00 PST.
- Bill as an overage/add-on at pilot rate (covering both reserved overhead + higher preemptable risk margin).
- Technical constraints: shards in that pool are already used for two enterprise pilots the week prior (week of 2027-04-28), so the earlier week is mostly free. We need a 72-hour provisioning SLA to patch kernels and map the allocation.

Asks: Marcus/Hannah — can infra/ops validate the 72-hour provisioning SLA and confirm whether autoscaling can be disabled for the priority band during the window without breaking other customers' SLOs? Also, Dev, please confirm if the pilot needs any nonstandard model variants pinned (quantized checkpoints) — that affects memory packing and slot sizing.

I'll draft a short MOP and send to Acme once we get ops confirmation.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jeffrey Turner <jeffrey.turner@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — infra impact and exception details

Marissa/Neha —

We can support a temporary priority band but need to enumerate a short list of exceptions and runbook changes. Key items:
1) Autoscale: we can pin two slots to a "pilot slice" with autoscale disabled for the 14:00-18:00 window. That requires a one-time kernel deployment and a KV cache warm-up.
2) Capacity: taking 2 slots out of the east-us pool will reduce available concurrency by ~9% for that window. There are currently two other reserved pilots scheduled in Q2 (internal schedule), but they are outside the requested week — I verified with the capacity calendar.
3) Monitoring & fallbacks: ops wants a fallback route to a compatible lower-spec model in case of a hardware failure; that needs to be wired into routing policy before provisioning.
4) Lead time: 72 hours is reasonable if we get sign-off and a short SOW and payment authorization. If Acme requests VPC peering + private control plane access, add 5 business days for networking.

Attachments: pool-topology-diagram.png (reference), draft MOP stub in related links.

Action items assigned:
- Hannah: confirm maintenance blackout for the requested day/time and sign the runbook.
- Dev: validate pinned model artifact sizing and any changes to quantization/packing.
- Marissa/Neha: get Acme to sign SOW and confirm the pilot start date window.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jeffrey Turner <jeffrey.turner@acme.ai>, Tony Liu <tony.liu@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — ops confirmation and conditional approval

All —

We validated the schedule against the maintenance calendar; no conflicting windows for the requested dates. Ops can provision the 2-slot priority band with the following conditions:
- We require the signed SOW and payment authorization at least 72 hours before the first reserved day.
- The priority band will be carved out of the east-us dedicated pool and autoscale will be disabled for the 14:00-18:00 window only; outside that window the capacity returns to the pool.
- We will implement a fallback model routing policy (lower-spec) — if that route is exercised more than 3 times in the pilot, we will pause the pilot and trigger a post-mortem.
- Network/VPC requirements: if Acme asks for private routing, expect an additional 5 business days for networking approvals.

Marissa/Neha: once you have the signed SOW, we can schedule the 72-hour provisioning slot.

Jeffrey/Tony: happy to hop on a short call if you want to narrow the SLA language.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Manager, Dedicated Platform
Redwood Inference
